notes:
Account summary: EchoFlow runs a cloud+on-prem platform for enterprise contact centers (voice + messaging). Strong mandate to add real-time agent assist (streaming suggestions) and automated ticket summarization. Primary driver = reduce AHT and increase FCR while keeping hallucination risk low.

Sales/AE notes: met 2026-02-12 with Head of Platform (Maria Gomez) + CTO (Evan Liu). They said: "Need sub-100ms suggestion latency at token-level for live agent UI" and "ability to call internal tools (CRM updates, macros) from suggestions with audit trail". Willing to pay for reserved capacity if latency and reliability proven.

Security/compliance: heavy requirements for audit logs, KMS, SAML SSO; preference to keep EU customer data in EU region (data residency). Security questionnaire returned 2026-01-29; following items flagged: endpoint hardening, egress rules for connectors, HSM/KMS specifics. Refer to drive doc Redwood_Security_FAQ_v2.pdf.

Technical concerns: voice channel streaming (partial transcripts) -> needs low-latency prefix caching and ability to stream partial suggestions while transcript still arriving. During campaign spikes they see 2-3x baseline concurrent agents (peaks up to ~4k concurrent live agents). They want automatic fallback routing to lower-cost models when capacity constrained but strict guardrails on hallucination and PII exposure.

Quotes and style: shorthand OK in notes. Focus is pragmatic: POC must include a 48h soak with synthetic spike and live baton handoff test.

requirements_summary:
Primary: real-time agent assist with streaming suggestions (token-level streaming), <100ms per-suggestion P95 under baseline; tolerate up to 300ms P95 during spikes but need graceful degradation. Must provide tool-calling with auditable events, function-call semantics, and deterministic fallbacks. Ticket summarization for post-call workflows (batch embeddings + short abstractive summary). Integration: Zendesk (voice+tickets), Salesforce, internal macros API. Observability needs: per-route latency and token-cost breakdown, trace links to transcripts.

Non-functional: reserved capacity options for peak events, VPC peering or on-prem connector for transcripts, encryption-at-rest with customer KMS, SOC2 attestation required.
integration_targets: Zendesk (voice streaming + ticket attach), Salesforce case updates, internal macro service (HTTP function-call), SSO via Okta/SAML. Voice provider: Twilio -> want demo of partial-transcript streaming into Redwood runtime.
